name: SoundDriver
note: the sound driver SMSG 3.07w (Jason Andersen / John Schappert, 8/17/1994) as IPL upload blocks; $CF001A sends it through $CF004B after SoundRAMClear; 94S SoundDriver is the program its SPCUpload sends, but this is a different driver

name: .init
note: sound RAM $1000; the start address of the stream: stack, ports, DSP set up from .dspregs/.dspvalues, tcall vectors copied, ready $7F on port 3, then .mainloop

name: .dspregs
note: sound RAM $1076; DSP registers set at init (read with Y from 8 down to 1)

name: .dspvalues
note: sound RAM $107E; their values

name: .tcallvectors
note: sound RAM $1086; 16 words copied to $FFC0: the tcall 15..0 handlers

name: .version
note: sound RAM $10A6; the string SMSG 3.07w Jason Andersen/John Schappert 8/17/1994, no terminator

name: .mainloop
note: sound RAM $0120; port 2 status, then .poll

name: .poll
note: sound RAM $0125; timer 0 count: run .tick that many times; else a command on port 3

name: .ticks
note: sound RAM $0130; calls .tick once per timer 0 count

name: .command
note: sound RAM $013C; command 1-$20 on port 3, arguments on ports 0-2, through .commands

name: .cmdcall
note: sound RAM $016E; call whose operand .command sets from .commands

name: .tick
note: sound RAM $0173; per timer tick: voice end flags, voice timers, one queued command, the sequencer

name: .queuecall
note: sound RAM $01E5; call whose operand the queue code sets from .commands

name: .eventcall
note: sound RAM $023B; call whose operand the sequencer sets from .events

name: .commands
note: sound RAM $04F3; 32 words: handlers of commands 1-$20 (the code reads it as .commands-2 + command * 2)

name: .events
note: sound RAM $0533; 4 words: handlers of music events $80-$83

name: .bootrom
note: sound RAM $053B; command 27: boot ROM on and jump to it, so the CPU can upload again

name: .voicebits
note: sound RAM $0AC4; 8 bytes: the bit of each voice

name: .voiceregs
note: sound RAM $0ACC; 8 bytes: the DSP register base of each voice

name: .pitchlo
note: sound RAM $0AD4; 12 bytes: low bytes of the semitone pitch table

name: .pitchhi
note: sound RAM $0AE0; 12 bytes: high bytes ($2C82 to $5405)

name: .sine
note: sound RAM $0AEC; 64 signed bytes: one sine period

name: spcQueueWrite
note: sound CPU RAM; write index of spcQueue (the queueing code at $06DD)

name: spcQueueRead
note: sound CPU RAM; read index of spcQueue (.tick)

name: spcArg0
note: sound CPU RAM; port 0 when a command came

name: spcArg1
note: sound CPU RAM; port 1 when a command came

name: spcArg2
note: sound CPU RAM; port 2 when a command came

name: spcCmdIndex
note: sound CPU RAM; command number * 2

name: spcControl
note: sound CPU RAM; value .command writes to SPC_CONTROL; init sets $20

name: spcENDX
note: sound CPU RAM; DSP_ENDX read at the last tick

name: spcStatus
note: sound CPU RAM; sent on port 2: bit 7 busy, bit 6 in .ticks

name: spcQueue
note: sound CPU RAM; 64-byte ring of 4-byte queued commands (arguments, then command); RAM under the boot ROM

name: spcTcallVectors
note: sound CPU RAM; the tcall vectors in RAM (boot ROM off)

name: SPC_T0OUT
note: sound CPU timer 0 counter

name: DSP_ENDX
note: DSP register: voices at the end of their sample

name: BoldFontGlyphs
note: 46 glyphs of 16 x 8 (32 bytes, 2bpp rows): 0-9, punctuation, A-Z; the text routine $C4BE34 gets it in $0C from $C4BC59, $C4BCD4, $C4BCF6, $C4BD16, $C4BE1A (flags $0E = 0 or $4000: 32 byte glyphs, lowercase codes as capitals)

name: ItalicFontGlyphs
note: 16 x 16 glyphs (64 bytes): 0-9, punctuation, A-Z (glyphs $00-$2A), the same set again for lowercase codes ($2B-$55); callers $C4BC37, $C4BD40, $C4BD7A, $C4BD99 with flags $0003 / $4003; its glyphs from $49 lie under ThinFontGlyphs

name: ThinFontGlyphs
note: 16 x 16 thin capitals; caller $C4BD57 with flags $0005 (64 byte glyphs, its own per-character table); glyphs $0D-$10 punctuation, $11-$2A A-Z; glyphs $00-$0C are ItalicFontGlyphs' $49-$55; ends where a packed set starts ($C03CF9, $C5ACBE)

name: WonCheckTiles
note: 48 4bpp tiles, packed format 2 ($0600 bytes): a WON label in two sizes, a check mark, framed boxes; $C5ACBE unpacks them to $7E:50DC and queues them for VRAM $0130; the routine at $C5ACAA has no direct caller, so the screen is not traced

name: WonCheckPalette
note: 16 colours; $C5ACED queues them to CGRAM $70 (palette 7) with WonCheckTiles

name: AwayUniformPalettes
note: 94S AwayUniformPalettes by purpose (dark jersey colours per team); here interleaved with HomeUniformPalettes, 64 bytes per team, 28 teams then one more pair; $C520C2 / $C55799 add team $17CB * 64 and queue CGRAM palette 3

name: HomeUniformPalettes
note: 94S HomeUniformPalettes by purpose (white jersey colours per team); 64 bytes per team; $C520AF / $C55786 add team $17C9 * 64 and queue CGRAM palette 4

name: DigitFontTiles
note: 15 4bpp tiles, packed format 2 ($01E0): 0-9 and D L C R X (the glyphs of 94S SPFsmallfont); $C5211F / $C556C9 unpack them and queue them for VRAM $6360

name: LinePieceTiles
note: 63 4bpp tiles, packed format 6 ($07E0): straight and diagonal line pieces and corners; $C52216 unpacks them to $7F:D02A, then $C539D7 builds a screen

name: BG3ScrollHDMA1

name: BG3ScrollHDMA2
